definition: A name that refers to a value stored in memory. Assign with =, e.g. x = 10.
The kind of a value: int, float, str, bool, or NoneType. Check it with type().
A whole number without a decimal point, e.g. 42. Type name: int.
A number with a decimal point, e.g. 3.14. Type name: float.
A sequence of characters in quotes. Indexed from 0; immutable; format with f-strings.
A value that is either True or False, used in conditions.
A special value meaning 'no value'. Functions without return give back None.
An ordered, mutable collection in square brackets. Items can be appended, removed or changed.
An ordered, immutable collection in parentheses. Once created, its items cannot change.
An unordered collection of key-value pairs in curly braces. Look values up by their key.
An unordered collection of unique items in curly braces. Duplicates are removed automatically.
A reusable block defined with def. It takes parameters and returns a result with return.
A name listed in a function definition that receives a value when the function is called.
A value passed to a function when calling it.
The result a function sends back with return. Without return, the result is None.
A small anonymous one-line function written with the lambda keyword.
Where a variable is visible: local inside a function, global outside it.
A blueprint for creating objects, defined with the class keyword.
An instance created from a class, holding its own data and methods.
A child class reusing a parent class's attributes and methods, optionally overriding them.
The constructor method of a class. It initializes a new object and runs automatically on creation.
The first parameter of a method. It refers to the object the method was called on.
A single Python file reused with import, e.g. import math.
A folder of modules, imported as one unit.
Python's package installer. pip install requests installs a package from PyPI.
An isolated folder for a project's packages, created with python -m venv .venv.
A runtime error object, e.g. ValueError or FileNotFoundError.
try holds code that might fail; except runs when a specific exception occurs; finally always runs.
A one-line expression that builds a list from a loop and an optional condition.
A function using yield that produces values lazily, one at a time, without storing them all.
A string prefixed with f that embeds values in curly braces, e.g. f'Hi, {name}'.
Leading spaces that define code blocks in Python, usually 4 spaces. Wrong indentation is an error.
Python's official style guide: 4-space indentation, snake_case names, readable spacing.
A triple-quoted string at the top of a module, class or function that documents it.
An optional annotation like def f(x: int) -> int that documents expected types.
Reading and writing files with open(), ideally inside a with block so the file closes automatically.
A block that sets up and cleans up a resource automatically, e.g. closing a file.
A built-in that loops with both index and value: for i, v in enumerate(items).
A built-in producing a sequence of numbers, e.g. range(3) gives 0, 1, 2.
